action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-VGCC P/Q-type 0.48 nmol/L and anti-SOX1 positive; AChR and MuSK negative
action_criteria.label: Order P/Q-type VGCC antibodies
action_criteria.rationale: Proximal leg weakness, reflexes that facilitate after effort, dry mouth and ocular-bulbar symptoms after SCLC point to LEMS; P/Q-type VGCC antibodies support it (Titulaer 2011). SOX1 adds little once the SCLC is known, so it is reported but not required.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Low baseline CMAPs with a slow-rate decrement and post-exercise facilitation of 139-157%
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation with a post-exercise study
action_criteria.rationale: Low baseline CMAPs with an increment of at least 60% after 10 s of maximal contraction establish a presynaptic transmission defect; brief exercise replaces painful 50 Hz stimulation (Oh 2005).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Increased jitter and blocking that improve at a higher stimulation rate
action_criteria.label: Single-fibre EMG only if the RNS were equivocal
action_criteria.rationale: The RNS is diagnostic; SFEMG is abnormal in any junction disorder and adds little here.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild cardiovagal impairment and reduced foot sudomotor output without orthostatic hypotension
action_criteria.label: Autonomic function testing if the autonomic involvement needs documenting
action_criteria.rationale: Dry mouth is reported; formal testing documents autonomic involvement but does not change the diagnosis or treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: New indeterminate right paratracheal node (0.9 cm short axis) and stable post-radiation fibrosis
action_criteria.label: Order contrast CT of the chest for recurrent SCLC
action_criteria.rationale: New LEMS after treated SCLC raises recurrence; CT of the thorax is the first screening study (EFNS 2011).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Hypermetabolic right paratracheal node (SUVmax 6.8) with no distant disease
action_criteria.label: Order FDG-PET because the CT is indeterminate
action_criteria.rationale: The CT shows only a subcentimetre new node; FDG-PET is the next screening study when CT is negative or equivocal and identifies the biopsy target (EFNS 2011).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Small cell carcinoma in the station 4R node (TTF-1, synaptophysin and chromogranin A positive)
action_criteria.label: Arrange EBUS sampling of the PET-avid paratracheal node
action_criteria.rationale: Histology confirms recurrence before oncology restarts treatment; EBUS of station 4R is the low-risk route.

action_criteria.label: Obtain a baseline ECG before amifampridine
action_criteria.rationale: The EU SmPC requires an ECG at initiation; QTc is the gate for amifampridine, and she has been taking ondansetron.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Ondansetron prolongs QT and is contraindicated with amifampridine (EU SmPC); seizure risk; dosing and ECG monitoring
action_criteria.label: Check amifampridine against her medicines
action_criteria.rationale: She takes ondansetron, a QT-prolonging drug that the EU SmPC lists as a contraindication to amifampridine; the check changes what she can be prescribed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on LEMS diagnosis, tumour screening and symptomatic treatment
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on LEMS
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose myasthenia gravis: low CMAPs with post-exercise facilitation and P/Q-type VGCC antibodies indicate LEMS, and AChR antibodies are negative.
Do not start amifampridine while she takes ondansetron or another QT-prolonging drug, or in a patient with epilepsy.

Avoid aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not accept a CT without a clear mass as excluding SCLC recurrence in new LEMS; FDG-PET and tissue are needed.
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to thoracic oncology for treatment of the recurrent small cell lung cancer; treating the tumour is the main treatment of paraneoplastic LEMS.

Stop ondansetron, then start amifampridine 15 mg/day in three divided doses after the baseline ECG, increasing by 5 mg every 4-5 days to effect (EU maximum 60 mg/day, 20 mg per dose), with clinical and ECG monitoring at initiation and yearly thereafter (EU SmPC).
Add pyridostigmine 30-60 mg three times daily if weakness persists on amifampridine; consider IVIG 2 g/kg if weakness remains disabling despite tumour treatment and symptomatic therapy.

Give her a list of drugs that worsen neuromuscular transmission (aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, IV magnesium) and tell the anaesthetist before any procedure, including EBUS (reduced non-depolarising neuromuscular blocker doses).
Offer early palliative care involvement alongside oncology treatment for recurrent SCLC.

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure or encephalopathy; EEG has no role in a neuromuscular junction disorder.
No CNS or leptomeningeal question; CSF has no role in LEMS.
Brain MRI last month showed no metastases and there is no new central sign.

accepted: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS), paraneoplastic, secondary to recurrent small cell lung cancer; anti-VGCC P/Q positive, anti-SOX1 positive
LEMS with small cell lung cancer

differential.key_features: AChR and MuSK negative; low baseline CMAPs with post-exercise facilitation and VGCC antibodies indicate a presynaptic disorder.
Explains the reduced sural SNAPs and toe vibration loss, but not proximal weakness, facilitating reflexes, diplopia or low CMAPs that facilitate after exercise.
Carboplatin and etoposide do not cause a myopathy with post-exercise CMAP facilitation or VGCC antibodies.
TSH and free T4 normal on levothyroxine.
Thoracic radiation could affect the brachial plexus but does not cause symmetric proximal leg weakness with facilitation.

key_clinical_evidence: Proximal leg-predominant weakness with reflexes that facilitate after brief contraction, dry mouth and mild ocular-bulbar symptoms after treated SCLC.
Anti-VGCC P/Q-type 0.48 nmol/L and anti-SOX1 positive; AChR negative.
RNS shows low baseline CMAPs, a 12-16% slow-rate decrement and 139-157% facilitation after 10 s of exercise (presynaptic pattern).
Chest CT shows only an indeterminate new 0.9 cm paratracheal node; FDG-PET shows it is hypermetabolic and EBUS confirms small cell carcinoma.
Ondansetron is a QT-prolonging drug that must be stopped before amifampridine; the baseline QTc is 441 ms.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: AChR-negative does not exclude LEMS; anti-VGCC is the discriminating test.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude 'NMJ disorder excluded' and miss LEMS.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: In new LEMS after SCLC a CT without a clear mass does not exclude recurrence; FDG-PET and tissue sampling are the next steps.
red_herrings.data_point: CT chest with only an indeterminate subcentimetre paratracheal node
red_herrings.intended_effect: Reassurance that SCLC is in remission and stop oncology workup.

sequence_constraints.reason: CT of the thorax is the first tumour-screening study; FDG-PET follows when CT is negative or equivocal (EFNS 2011).
Imaging identifies the node before it is sampled.
The baseline QTc informs the amifampridine safety check.

contraindications: Amifampridine: contraindicated in epilepsy, uncontrolled asthma, congenital long QT syndrome and with QT-prolonging medicines (EU SmPC).
interactions: Ondansetron: prolongs the QT interval in a dose-dependent manner; the EU SmPC contraindicates amifampridine with medicines that have a known potential to prolong the QT interval. Stop the combination or choose an antiemetic without QT liability.
warnings: Amifampridine lowers the seizure threshold in a dose-dependent manner.
Clinical and ECG monitoring at initiation and yearly thereafter (EU SmPC); ECG at once if symptoms suggest arrhythmia.
Dosing (EU SmPC): start 15 mg/day in three divided doses, increase by 5 mg every 4-5 days, maximum 60 mg/day and 20 mg per single dose. Perioral and distal paraesthesias are common.

Neuromuscular junction disorder: avoid aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, IV magnesium and calcium channel blockers where possible; non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers need reduced doses with quantitative monitoring.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis. PR 168 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 441 ms (Bazett). No ST-T changes.
ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 78. Normal intervals (QTc 441 ms). Normal ECG.

labs.interpretation: Anti-VGCC P/Q-type antibody 0.48 nmol/L (elevated) and anti-SOX1 antibody positive. Anti-AChR and anti-MuSK not detected. CBC, electrolytes including calcium and magnesium, creatinine and thyroid function within reference ranges. P/Q-type VGCC antibodies are found in most patients with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome and SOX1 antibodies are associated with small cell lung cancer; clinical correlation recommended.

Neuromuscular_Antibodies.test: Anti-SOX1 antibody (line blot, confirmed by cell-based assay)

Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome diagno.query: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: LEMS presents with proximal weakness, autonomic dysfunction and areflexia; P/Q-type VGCC antibodies are found in about 85-90% and about half of patients have small cell lung cancer.
results.source: Titulaer MJ, Lang B, Verschuuren JJ. Lancet Neurol 2011;10:1098-1107

results.finding: CT of the thorax is the first screening study in LEMS; FDG-PET is added when CT is negative, with repeat screening every 3-6 months for 2 years.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Eur J Neurol 2011;18:19-e3

results.finding: A post-exercise CMAP increment of 60% or more is a sensitive and specific electrodiagnostic marker of LEMS.
results.source: Oh SJ et al. Muscle Nerve 2005;32:515-520

Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome diagno.summary: Titulaer MJ et al. (Lancet Neurol 2011;10:1098-1107) describe LEMS as proximal weakness, autonomic dysfunction and areflexia with P/Q-type VGCC antibodies in about 85-90%; about half of patients have small cell lung cancer. SOX1 antibodies favour an associated SCLC. CT of the thorax is the first screening study and FDG-PET is added when CT is negative, with repeat screening every 3-6 months for 2 years (EFNS 2011). Amifampridine is the first-line symptomatic treatment.

specialized_test.impression: 1. Low baseline CMAP amplitudes in all tested motor nerves with a 12-16% decrement at 3 Hz and post-exercise facilitation of 139-157% after 10 s of maximal contraction. These findings indicate a presynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission. 2. Reduced sural SNAPs, consistent with a length-dependent sensory axonal neuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive proximal leg weakness 6 months after completing SCLC chemotherapy

past_medical_history: Small cell lung cancer (limited stage, diagnosed 10 months ago, completed 4 cycles carboplatin/etoposide + thoracic radiation, in surveillance)

social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 45 pack-years, quit 1 year ago

patient.history_present_illness: A 68-year-old woman with recently completed treatment for limited-stage small cell lung cancer presented with 3 months of progressive proximal leg weakness. She completed 4 cycles of carboplatin/etoposide chemotherapy with concurrent thoracic radiation 6 months ago and achieved a complete radiographic response. At her most recent surveillance visit, she reported difficulty rising from chairs (she now needs both arm rests to push herself to standing) and difficulty climbing stairs. She initially attributed this to deconditioning after cancer treatment. Her oncologist referred her to rehabilitation, which helped minimally. She has also noted intermittent double vision when driving and reading, occurring in the afternoons but not in the mornings. She mentioned her mouth seems dry most of the time. Over the past 3 months, she has had mild difficulty chewing and her voice becomes nasal in the evenings. She denies sensory symptoms in her hands but has mild numbness in her feet (known carboplatin neuropathy). She denies dysphagia, ptosis in the morning, or respiratory symptoms. Her last surveillance CT of the chest, 3 months ago, showed post-radiation changes only, and a brain MRI ordered by her oncologist last month showed no metastases. She was referred to neurology with the working diagnosis of either carboplatin peripheral neuropathy or paraneoplastic syndrome from SCLC.

neurological_exam.additional: No respiratory distress. Dry mouth noted. No orthostatic symptoms currently. Proximal leg weakness is the dominant feature.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: No ptosis at rest. On sustained upgaze, subtle right ptosis at 80 seconds. No diplopia on casual testing. Horizontal diplopia reported on sustained rightward gaze for >60 seconds. Pupils equal, reactive. No facial weakness at rest. Voice slightly nasal at end of 10-minute examination.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly wide-based. Difficulty rising from chair.
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal leg weakness: hip flexors 3+/5 bilaterally. Proximal arm: deltoids 4-/5. Distal 5/5. Hip flexor strength improves briefly after a few seconds of maximal effort, then declines with sustained effort.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps and patellar reflexes trace, ankle reflexes absent; patellar reflexes become 1+ immediately after 10 seconds of maximal quadriceps contraction. Plantar downgoing.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild decrease to vibration at the toes bilaterally (known carboplatin neuropathy).

physical_exam.general: Weight 63.5 kg, height 162 cm. No respiratory distress. Dry oral mucosa.
